Cuts preserve the original sloped sockets.
Grey outlines: indexed pavement, barriers, concrete, and supports.
Coloured tile fills: exclusive construction ownership.
Blue: lower roads. Orange: upper roads.
Grey: ground roads. Green: pedestrian paths.
Retain: highway and slip lanes remain one stamp.
Reusable as is: the four sloped high boundaries.
Requires bounded redesign: new flat ground cuts, implemented.
Unverified: a universal graded building-block family.
Obstacle: Jersey barriers and supports must fit in 3D.
Constraint: every piece has fixed absolute heights.
New circular ramp and terminal sections: R40.
Cut coordinates (X, Y tiles); actual PATH height
The highway stamp has 27 owned tiles. The R40 attachments add 35; the reference assembly has 62 unique tiles.
Connectors record slopes and angles. Physical seam, clearance, and game checks remain separate evidence.
Actual saved PATH centre-lines; structural triangle projections; no inferred draggable/FLEX or arbitrary-height behaviour.
